title: Story: The Emperor's New Clothes
summary: Andersen's famous tale: two tricksters "weave" invisible clothes for the emperor, and only a child tells the truth. Told in the present tense with short, simple sentences.
phrases: He spends a lot of money on it.
You should always tell the truth.
Honesty is more important than fear.
phraseNotes: so tun, als ob = to pretend
lines: The Emperor's New Clothes.
In a great kingdom there lives an emperor.
He loves beautiful clothes.
He buys new clothes every day and spends a great deal of money on them.
Every morning he puts on new clothes.
In the afternoon he puts on different clothes again.
His clothes matter more to him than many other things.
One day two men come to the city.
They say that they are very good weavers.
They can make special clothes.
The emperor is delighted and invites the two men to the palace.
The men explain:
"Our clothes are very special.
Stupid people cannot see these clothes.
People who don't do their work well can't see these clothes either."
The emperor thinks: "That's wonderful.
This way I can tell clever people from stupid ones."
So he gives the men a lot of gold, silk and expensive thread.
The men put two looms in a room.
But they don't really work.
The looms are empty.
There is no fabric.
Still they move their hands and pretend to be working.
After a few days the emperor wants to see the fabric.
But he is also afraid.
He thinks: "What happens if I can't see the fabric?"
So he sends an old minister to the weavers.
The minister looks at the looms.
But … he sees no fabric.
He thinks: "Oh no, I can't see anything. Am I stupid?"
He doesn't want to say so.
The men ask: "Do you like the fabric?"
The minister answers: "Yes, of course, it's very beautiful.
The colours are wonderful."
Then he goes back to the emperor and says: "The fabric really is very beautiful."
The emperor is delighted.
Later he sends a second official.
This man sees no fabric either.
But he is afraid too.
So he says: "The fabric is gorgeous."
Now the emperor wants to see the fabric himself.
He goes to the weavers and sees the empty looms.
He thinks: "I can't see anything. Nobody must know that."
The men point at the empty loom and say: "Look at the beautiful colours!
Do you see the fine pattern?"
The emperor sees nothing, but he says: "Yes, really very beautiful."
After that he gives the men even more gold.
A few days later the men say: "The new clothes are ready."
They pretend to give the emperor the clothes.
Then they help him get dressed.
But the emperor isn't wearing any clothes.
He is just standing there in his underwear.
The men say: "The clothes are very light. That's why you can't feel them."
The emperor nods.
The servants say nothing either. They are afraid.
That day there is a big parade.
The emperor walks through the streets.
Lots of people stand there and see him.
But nobody tells the truth. Everyone is afraid.
They say how beautiful the new clothes are and that the emperor looks wonderful.
Only a little child shouts loudly: "But the emperor is naked!"
The people look at the emperor.
At first they are silent.
Then some people begin to laugh.
Soon lots of people are laughing.
Now they all tell the truth: "The child is right. The emperor is naked."
More and more people laugh and say: "The emperor is naked!"
The emperor hears everything.
Now he knows that everyone knows the truth.
He is very ashamed.
But he keeps walking.
The servants run behind him.
They are still pretending to carry the long clothes.
Since that day people have remembered this story.
They understand: you should always tell the truth.
Honesty is more important than fear.
topics: Retell the story: what happens to the emperor?
Honesty: when is it hard to tell the truth?
My clothes: what do you like to wear?

focus.title: Telling a story in the present
points: This tale is told in the present tense — easier for level A2: Er liebt schöne Kleidung. · Eines Tages kommen zwei Männer.
Irregular verbs change their stem with du and er: geben → er gibt · sehen → er sieht · laufen → sie laufen
In a main clause the verb is always second: Jeden Morgen zieht er neue Kleidung an.
Compare with the past: er liebt → er liebte · er sieht → er sah

focus.title: Separable verbs
points: anziehen: Er zieht neue Kleidung an. · ausgeben: Er gibt viel Geld aus.
einladen: Der Kaiser lädt die Männer in den Palast ein.
ansehen: Der Minister sieht die Webstühle an. · aussehen: Er sieht wunderbar aus.
The prefix goes to the end; with a modal verb the verb stays whole: Er möchte den Stoff ansehen.

focus.title: Pretending
points: so tun, als ob + a clause with the verb at the end = to pretend that …
Sie tun so, als ob sie arbeiten. — they pretend they are working
Sie tun so, als ob sie dem Kaiser die Kleidung geben.
At a higher level with Konjunktiv II: als ob sie arbeiten würden

focus.title: Linking sentences
points: dass: the verb goes to the end: Sie sagen, dass sie gute Weber sind.
wenn (if): Was passiert, wenn ich den Stoff nicht sehen kann?
deshalb (that's why) comes first, the verb right after it: Deshalb gibt er den Männern viel Gold.
trotzdem (still, anyway) works the same: Trotzdem bewegen sie ihre Hände.

focus.title: Verbs with the dative
points: gefallen: Gefällt Ihnen der Stoff? (do you like it?)
helfen: Sie helfen ihm beim Anziehen.
geben + Dativ (to whom) + Akkusativ (what): Er gibt den Männern viel Gold.
The dative plural always adds -n: den Männern, den Webern

cues.title: Questions about the story
items: Why doesn't the minister say anything?
